chunks: From him, from Ali, from his father, from Yahya ibn Abi Imran, from Yunus, from Abu Abdillah ibn Sulayman, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no man who grants security to a man under his protection (dhimmah) and then kills him, except that he will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying the banner of treachery.'

key_terms.ذِمَّةٍ: Protection or security granted to a person

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of killing someone you granted security to?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the gravity of violating *aman* (security/guarantee), a concept deeply rooted in pre-Islamic and Islamic jurisprudence as a binding social contract. The imagery of carrying the 'banner of treachery' signifies a public, humiliating mark of betrayal on the Day of Judgment, underscoring that breaking a pledge of safety is not merely a legal breach but a major spiritual sin. This narration reinforces the Shia scholarly view that *aman* granted by an individual carries the same weight as that granted by the Imam or the state, making it a sacred trust.
